title: add content-disposition/metadata guards and per-tool payload quotas for multipart uploads
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Tool/file attachments used by the OpenAI-compatible tool-calling surface were allowing poorly formed multipart uploads and oversized payloads which caused streaming stalls and OOMs in the serving runtime. This PR introduces explicit guards around Content-Disposition and file metadata, per-tool and per-account payload quotas for multipart/form-data parts, improved multipart boundary handling to avoid partial-read hangs in stream mode, and small compatibility tweaks so the OpenAI compatibility layer surfaces a stable `files` metadata object for tool calls. Changes are intentionally conservative: they add validation and soft-failure modes (400 + diagnostics) by default and an env flag to opt into hard rejection for stricter enterprise deployments. The description below summarizes goals, changes, test coverage, and rollout plan.
commits: feat(api): validate Content-Disposition and filename charset across multipart parts
fix(stream): avoid blocking partial reads by enforcing boundary lookahead and backpressure tokens
feat(quota): implement per-tool and per-account multipart-part size quotas and aggregate request limits
chore(compat): emit stable files metadata in OpenAI compatibility responses for tool attachments
test: add integration tests for malformed boundaries, oversized part, and content-type mismatches
docs: add runtime config docs and migration notes

review_thread: Jordan Patel: Can we make the default per-part quota conservative for hosted API customers? It should not break common plugin/tool attachments (images, small files).
Avery Chen: Yes — default per_part is 5MB and aggregate 50MB for hosted; documented and configurable via runtime_defaults.yaml. Enterprise customers can set stricter values.
Nina Suresh: The streaming fix looks good but please add a test that reproduces the partial-boundary hang we saw in perf-canary PR. I left a nit in boundary_reader.rs.
Avery Chen: Added the perf-canary style test and tightened the timeout logic; replied to the nit with a small refactor to make lookahead non-blocking.
Mateo Alvarez: Approving after CI passes. One last ask: include a brief note in the OpenAI-compat release notes about the `files` metadata shape so downstream SDKs can adapt.
Avery Chen: Added release_notes and a console docs entry per request. Thanks!

release_notes: Added safer multipart handling for tool/file attachments: validates Content-Disposition/filename, enforces per-part and per-request quotas (defaults: 5MB per part, 50MB aggregate for hosted), hardens multipart boundary streaming to prevent partial-read hangs, and exposes a stable `files` metadata object in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Configurable via services/config/runtime_defaults.yaml and runtime env flags. Backwards-compatible soft-failure mode used by default.
